rationale_evidence.anchor: Nexus as reference domain, not merely an example.
rationale_evidence.statement: Chooses Nexus as the vertical-slice subject because existing KnowledgeOS work already covers infrastructure discovery, version info, repository/blob-store info, runtime info, network info, migration requirements, governance questions, and architecture/change-management concerns — spanning Business/Architecture/Infrastructure/Security/Operations/Governance knowledge; but requires starting with Read->Analyze->Verify, not Agent->Production->Modify Nexus, to prove the semantic/assurance architecture without unnecessary operational risk.

rationale_evidence.anchor: WS1 → {WS2, WS3} → WS4 → WS5 → WS6 → WS7. Do not scale agent access before authority is defined. Governance → Assurance. Verdict → Evidence.
rationale_evidence.statement: Presents the workstream dependency graph and justifies the ordering: Agent Integration is not first because 'if the semantic foundation is unstable, the agents simply automate ambiguity' (do not scale agent access before authority is defined); the Graph is not first because a graph of poorly defined semantics produces 'fast confusion,' needing stable identities/ownership/relationships first; Governance is early because it defines ExpectedState (without which assurance has nothing authoritative to compare against, Governance->Assurance); Evidence is early because without it Verification becomes a bare assertion (Verdict->Evidence required).

## Rationale
Chooses Nexus as the vertical-slice subject because existing KnowledgeOS work already covers infrastructure discovery, version info, repository/blob-store info, runtime info, network info, migration requirements, governance questions, and architecture/change-management concerns — spanning Business/Architecture/Infrastructure/Security/Operations/Governance knowledge; but requires starting with Read->Analyze->Verify, not Agent->Production->Modify Nexus, to prove the semantic/assurance architecture without unnecessary operational risk [S1045]. Presents the workstream dependency graph and justifies the ordering: Agent Integration is not first because 'if the semantic foundation is unstable, the agents simply automate ambiguity' (do not scale agent access before authority is defined); the Graph is not first because a graph of poorly defined semantics produces 'fast confusion,' needing stable identities/ownership/relationships first; Governance is early because it defines ExpectedState (without which assurance has nothing authoritative to compare against, Governance->Assurance); Evidence is early because without it Verification becomes a bare assertion (Verdict->Evidence required) [S1045].

NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE

- `[S1044]` types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Defines a six-phase evolution sequence (not implementing all twenty work packages simultaneously), with each phase's rationale: Phase 1 establishes Identity/Ownership/Authority/Validity (without which the graph merely connects ambiguous objects); Phase 2 formalizes Decision/Policy/Exception/Claim with documents becoming projections; Phase 3 formalizes Evidence/Observation/Rule/Verification/Finding, connecting existing checks; Phase 4 introduces the Assurance Graph and Context Service once underlying semantics are stable (ordering important); Phase 5 connects Agent->Action->Authorization->Execution for governed agentic engineering; Phase 6 makes KnowledgeOS a subject of its own assurance model for continuous architecture governance." (anchor: "CURRENT{Agents,Governance,Checks} → FORMALIZATION{Authority,Evidence,Rules} → RELATIONSHIP → ASSURANCE GRAPH → GOVERNED CONTEXT → GOVERNED AGENT → AUTHORIZED ACTION → EVIDENCE → VERIFICATION → GOVE...")

(anchor: "Documents → Machine-addressable semantic knowledge. AI Agent → Governed Engineering Actor. Compliance → Continuous Engineering Assurance.")
- `[S1044]` types=[RESTATEMENT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Step 143 verdict: the six most important semantic changes, after which existing Claude/Codex tooling, registry, deterministic checks, hooks, session logging, and engineering integrations can be progressively connected rather than replaced." - `[S1045]` types=[PRINCIPLE] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "States the central roadmap rule and the full first-vertical-slice chain (Governed Decision->Applicable Rule->Governed Agent Context->Agent Recommendation->Action Request->Authorization->Execution->Evidence->Verification->Finding->Governance), 'the smallest slice that demonstrates the actual architectural thesis.'" (anchor: "Do not build KnowledgeOS horizontally. Build one complete governed engineering loop.")
- `[S1045]` types=[ARGUMENT] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "Chooses Nexus as the vertical-slice subject because existing KnowledgeOS work already covers infrastructure discovery, version info, repository/blob-store info, runtime info, network info, migration requirements, governance questions, and architecture/change-management concerns — spanning Business/Architecture/Infrastructure/Security/Operations/Governance knowledge; but requires starting with Read->Analyze->Verify, not Agent->Production->Modify Nexus, to prove the semantic/assurance architecture without unnecessary operational risk." (anchor: "Nexus as reference domain, not merely an example.")

(anchor: "Vertical Slice 0: Can KnowledgeOS determine the current governed state of Nexus and explain the evidence supporting that state?")

- `[S1045]` types=[EXPERIMENT, FORMALIZATION] scope=OBJECT — "Vertical Slice 3 introduces the action-request/authorization boundary with three distinguished states." (anchor: "Vertical Slice 5: Action → Evidence → Verification → PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, with failure raising FindingRaised.")

- `[S1045]` types=[PRINCIPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "WS2 (Governance & Knowledge) migration principle: formalize Decision/Policy/Exception/Claim by extracting semantic objects from existing documents and linking back to the original artifact, preserving evidence/provenance rather than mechanical migration." - `[S1045]` types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "WS7 (Self-Assurance): once the first loop works, KnowledgeOS becomes subject to its own assurance rules via six example self-checks."
